title: Hamiltonian Thresholds for Objective Records
abstract: Classical objectivity requires an environment to witness a pointer value, not merely to decohere it. We derive microscopic Hamiltonian laws for this distinction. Exact QND product monitoring yields a certified two-edge strong-Darwinism window: sufficient witnesses cross the optimal record-discrimination edge while retaining an unobserved complement that crosses the residual-coherence edge. Under additional regularity assumptions, the supplement gives converse bounds at the same logarithmic scale. For controlled-phase monitors, environmental asymmetry gives a single-fragment information bound, a redundancy converse, and, in efficient i.i.d. streams, an achievable block-capacity law for redundant witnesses. A finite-temperature spin-phase bath shows the physical separation: hot probes can decohere efficiently while losing the local asymmetry needed for objective witnesses.
summary: This theoretical work establishes Hamiltonian laws defining 'objective records' of quantum information by requiring two complementary conditions on environmental monitoring: sufficient distinguishability (record edge) and residual coherence erasure (dephasing edge). It shows that objective witnessing is windowed, not monotonic, in the size of the observed environment fragment.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental distinction between quantum decoherence (local invisibility) and true 'objective records' of quantum information, which require multiple independent environmental witnesses.
main_result: Objective record certification requires satisfying two complementary Hamiltonian thresholds: a lower 'record edge' related to distinguishability and an upper 'surplus-dephasing edge' related to residual coherence.
method: The analysis derives microscopic Hamiltonian laws by quantifying information content using metrics like Pointer Holevo Information, Pointer Discord, and the local strong-QD deficit ($\Delta SQD$).
model_or_system: The model uses a fragmented environment architecture interacting with a system via exact QND product monitoring. A specific physical example analyzed is the Tilted Thermal Spin-Phase Bath.
key_observables: Pointer Holevo Information ($\chi_{\Pi}$), Pointer Discord ($D_{\Pi}$), Local strong-QD deficit ($\Delta SQD$), Record Exponent ($C_{rec}(F)$), and Surplus-Dephasing Exponent ($C_{dec}(F)$).
important_parameters: The required accuracy $\epsilon$, the fragment size $m$ relative to total size $N$, and temperature $T$ (in physical examples).
main_assumptions: The results rely on additional regularity assumptions, assuming exact QND product monitoring, and utilizing i.i.d. stream models for capacity bounds.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the certified two-edge observer window in an i.i.d. binary pure-probe model and show how temperature affects this window in the spin-phase bath.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining objective records via Hamiltonian laws, deriving the two necessary complementary exponents ($C_{rec}$ and $C_{dec}$), establishing the resulting finite observer window, and finally determining capacity bounds using these thresholds for i.i.d. streams.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous, microscopic criteria (Hamiltonian thresholds) for when quantum information is objectively recorded in an environment, which has implications for understanding measurement processes beyond simple decoherence models relevant to open quantum systems theory.
